speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. To understand the extent of your ocular involvement, I will need to perform an exam. Please look straight ahead while I check your visual acuity in both eyes. REQUEST TEST: Best_Corrected_Vision

speaker: Doctor
text: The visual acuity test returned normal readings, which is interesting given your complaint of decreased vision. Since you are seeing black spots in your right eye, can you describe if these spots float, move with your eye, or are fixed in one place?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and fungal esophagitis raises concern for an opportunistic infection or tumor recurrence in the eye. Given your complaints of black spots and vision loss, can you tell me if you have noticed any floaters or flashes of light? REQUEST TEST: Fluorescein_Angiography; REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_Photo_Right_Eye

speaker: Doctor
text: The fluorescein angiography and fundus photos have been reviewed. The images reveal multiple yellowish-white retinal lesions with overlying vitritis in the right eye, consistent with infectious retinitis. Given your history of AIDS, Kaposi's sarcoma, and recent fungal esophagitis, have you recently received any treatment for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) or have you been exposed to anyone with a similar eye infection?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundus images showing yellowish-white retinal lesions with vitritis and your history of AIDS are highly suggestive of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. Given your recent fungal esophagitis, we must also rule out fungal endophthalmitis. Do you have a history of prior CMV retinitis treatment, and have you had any recent episodes of monocular vision loss or floaters? REQUEST TEST: PCR_CMV_Retinal_Wash

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CMV DNA detected in retinal wash fluid, viral load 450,000 copies/mL

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis. The detection of high viral load CMV DNA in the retinal wash, combined with the characteristic yellowish-white retinal lesions and vitritis seen on your fundus photos, confirms this diagnosis.
